projects.name: Readmory
projects.headline: A second home for what you read.
projects.description: Books, highlights, and reading history in one local-first workspace. Built for Kobo, KOReader, and Kobalt.
projects.imageAlt: Readmory showing the owner’s actual Kobo library, local book covers, and reading activity.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Reading records live across devices, databases, and annotation files. I wanted a place to connect books, highlights, and personal reflections.

story.title: What I built
story.text: A browser-based workspace that imports reader databases, keeps a local library, connects ideas across books, and exports notes and backups.

story.title: The engineering
story.text: Reader-specific imports preserve source identity. Repeated imports update existing records. Timed sessions, inferred intervals, and aggregate counters remain distinct.

story.title: The tradeoff
story.text: Local-first storage avoids a server library, but browser data can be cleared. Backups matter. Optional metadata enrichment is disclosed separately.

projects.caption: Real Kobo library. Captured in Readmory.

projects.name: Aegis
projects.headline: A more personal way to explore Taiwan.
projects.description: A regional trip planner connecting a searchable places library, maps, and source-grounded AI suggestions.
projects.imageAlt: Aegis Taiwan trip-planning prototype with a regional trip brief and places library.

story.title: The idea
story.text: Turn a trip brief into a useful starting point, with places a person can inspect on a map rather than an itinerary with no sources.

story.title: What I built
story.text: A searchable Taiwan places library, a regional planning flow, an OpenStreetMap view, and a bounded AI planning workflow.

story.title: The boundary
story.text: This is a local prototype. Retrieval is lexical, source records can age or overlap, and travel times, costs, and opening hours are estimates to verify.

patents.title: AI-based Abnormal Behavior Detection System for Elevators
patents.officialTitle: An abnormal human behavior detection system applicable to different camera viewpoints in elevator
patents.summary: Detecting abnormal passenger behavior across different elevator camera viewpoints.
patents.description: The system extracts 2D body features from a passenger image, reconstructs a 3D reference, and estimates a better viewing angle. It then projects the transformed reference onto a plane perpendicular to the ground and applies a behavior-detection model.
